stimulus.text: Martin Waldseemuller's world map, published in 1507, was the first map to use the name America for the lands across the Atlantic Ocean. It shows the western lands as a separate landmass. The portrait of Amerigo Vespucci stands beside one globe at the top of the map, and the portrait of the ancient geographer Ptolemy stands beside the other globe.
stimulus.source_note: Waldseemuller map, 1507, public domain; Library of Congress.

stem: Why did Waldseemuller name the western lands America, after Amerigo Vespucci?

options.text: Vespucci paid for the printing of the map in Saint-Die.
The Spanish crown ordered the name to honor a royal favorite.
Columbus asked that the lands be named for Vespucci.
Vespucci argued the lands were a new world, and mapmakers agreed.
